purpose: Prevent duplicate/stale game-development CI and cold-start waste while preserving native Windows authority, cross-platform technical evidence, security posture, deterministic governance and service-runner-safe local handoffs.

toolchain_lifecycle.rule: Normal persistent self-hosted jobs validate desired toolchain state first. Exact valid state is reused; partial drift repairs only the affected component; version or integrity mismatch rebuilds that component. A clean room is explicit/manual rather than the default for every commit.

windows_authority_rule: Use Windows only for behavior that actually requires Windows: native validation, Windows export/runtime behavior, Authenticode/trust boundaries or Windows alpha packaging. Repository identity, provenance and platform-independent static checks run on Linux. Prefer one Windows authority job per PR head and reuse one verified export for downstream Windows evidence.
handoff_rule: Service runners may create validated unsigned payloads and prepare-command files only below %PUBLIC%\NOVI. They must not assume write access to %PUBLIC%\Desktop, a human user's Desktop, Start Menu, certificate store or per-user Programs directory. Signing, installation and user-shell integration occur only after control passes to the interactive user.
adoption_rule: Every NOVI-family game repository copies this contract, tools/ci/check_game_ci_contract.py and the runner toolchain ensure scripts byte-for-byte. Future games extend project-specific tests, not these invariants.
